t.7.70.1: Having heard that most wondrous speech of Agastya, Rāghava, out of reverence and out of amazement, began to question him further.
t.7.70.2: O blessed one, how is that dreadful forest, where Śveta, the king of Vidarbha, performs austerities, devoid of beasts and birds?
t.7.70.3: The forest became devoid of living creatures, empty and forsaken by men, and he entered it to practise austerities. I wish to hear of this in truth.
t.7.70.4: Having heard Rāma's words, so full of curiosity, the supremely radiant one began to speak.
t.7.70.5: Long ago, in the Kṛta Age, O Rāma, Manu was the lord who wielded the rod of punishment; his son was the great Ikṣvāku, who increased the glory of the lineage.
t.7.70.6: Having installed that son, invincible on earth, in the ancestral kingdom, he said, “Become the founder of royal dynasties upon the earth.”
t.7.70.7: "So be it," the son promised his father, O Rāghava. Then Manu, supremely delighted, spoke once more.
t.7.70.8: I am pleased, and without doubt you are a doer of supremely noble deeds. Protect your subjects by means of the rod of punishment, but do not inflict punishment without cause.
t.7.70.9: The punishment that is brought down upon men who are offenders, that punishment, when released according to rule, leads the king to heaven.
t.7.70.10: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, be diligent in the use of punishment, my dear son; for as you do so, supreme dharma will be yours in the world.
t.7.70.11: Having thus given his son many instructions with earnest care, Manu, delighted, went to heaven, to the unsurpassed world of Brahmā.
t.7.70.12: When he had departed to heaven, Ikṣvāku of boundless splendour became absorbed in anxious thought, wondering, "How shall I beget sons?"
t.7.70.13: Through those various deeds of many forms, the righteous-souled son of Manu begot a hundred sons, who were like the sons of the gods.
t.7.70.15: His father named that son of little vigor Daṇḍa, thinking, “Surely the blow of the rod of punishment will fall upon his body.”
t.7.70.14: Dear Raghunandana, the youngest of all of them was foolish and unlearned, and he did not obey his elder brothers.
t.7.70.16: Seeing that terrible fault in his son, O Rāghava, he gave him a kingdom between the Vindhya and the Śaivala, O subduer of enemies.
t.7.70.17: That Daṇḍa became king there, on a lovely mountain slope, and, O Rāma, he founded a matchless, unsurpassed city.
t.7.70.18: And he gave the city the name Madhumanta, O lord, and he chose Uśanas, of excellent vows, as his family priest.
t.7.70.19: Thus that king, together with his family priest, ruled that kingdom, which was filled with joyful people, like the kingdom of the king of the gods in heaven.
